item.title: Egypt seeks to boost trade exchange, expand access for products to Iraqi market
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Mohamed Farid, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, held a meeting with Qahtan Taha Khalaf, Ambassador of Iraq to Egypt and Iraq’s Permanent Representative to the League of Arab States, to discuss ways to strengthen investment and trade relations between the two countries and explore areas of mutual cooperation, as part of preparations for the […]
item.content:encoded:
Mohamed Farid, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, held a meeting with Qahtan Taha Khalaf, Ambassador of Iraq to Egypt and Iraq’s Permanent Representative to the League of Arab States, to discuss ways to strengthen investment and trade relations between the two countries and explore areas of mutual cooperation, as part of preparations for the meetings of the Egyptian-Iraqi Joint Committee.

 

The meeting explored opportunities to increase trade exchange, expand access for Egyptian products to the Iraqi market, and support the participation of Egyptian companies in construction, building and reconstruction projects. Discussions also covered expanding cooperation in sectors of mutual interest ahead of the Joint Committee meetings.

 

Farid stressed Egypt’s commitment to translating its historic relations with Iraq into economic partnerships and tangible projects. He highlighted the production capabilities and competitiveness of Egyptian companies across various sectors, as well as their potential to boost exports and strengthen Egypt’s presence in the Iraqi market.

 

The minister also discussed the possibility of organising visits for Iraqi delegations to Egyptian factories to familiarise them with their production capabilities, thereby supporting the establishment of sustainable trade relations between companies in both countries.

 

The meeting also explored opportunities to expand the presence of Egyptian pharmaceutical products in the Iraqi market and facilitate their registration procedures in coordination with the relevant authorities. Discussions covered the possibility of organising a specialised exhibition to promote Egyptian pharmaceutical products and establishing mechanisms to help companies understand regulatory requirements and identify opportunities for expansion in the Iraqi market.

 

Furthermore, the two sides discussed opportunities to expand cooperation in non-banking financial services, capital markets, insurance and reinsurance, support the expansion of Egyptian companies in Iraq, and promote the exchange of expertise between regulatory authorities and relevant institutions in both countries.

 

For his part, the Iraqi Ambassador proposed establishing a permanent exhibition for Egyptian products in Iraq, with the possibility of providing a suitable venue for this purpose. The initiative would help broaden the reach of Egyptian products and facilitate their access to Iraqi consumers at competitive prices.

 

Khalaf also stressed Iraq’s readiness to provide Egyptian companies with information on projects and tenders, strengthen communication between institutions and businesses in both countries, and organise reciprocal visits for businesspeople and investors to explore available cooperation opportunities.

item.title: Egypt moves to regulate mobile phone market, curb price increases
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly has directed relevant ministries to prepare a comprehensive study to regulate the mobile phone market and ensure devices are available to consumers at affordable prices, as the government seeks to deepen local manufacturing and increase domestic production. Madbouly chaired a meeting on Sunday to review measures aimed at expanding Egypt’s mobile […]
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly has directed relevant ministries to prepare a comprehensive study to regulate the mobile phone market and ensure devices are available to consumers at affordable prices, as the government seeks to deepen local manufacturing and increase domestic production.

Madbouly chaired a meeting on Sunday to review measures aimed at expanding Egypt’s mobile phone manufacturing industry and addressing recent concerns over what he described as excessive price increases in the local market.

The meeting was attended by Minister of Communications and Information Technology Raafat Hindi, Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem, Consumer Protection Agency Head Ibrahim El-Segini, Egyptian Competition Authority Head Mahmoud Momtaz, and representatives of relevant government entities.

Madbouly said the government had been working with various authorities to attract international manufacturers and encourage further investment in Egypt, with the aim of localising the industry, increasing production capacity, meeting domestic demand at competitive prices and boosting exports.

He noted that mobile phones had become an essential commodity for citizens, stressing the need to take immediate and long-term measures to ensure their availability at reasonable prices.

According to Cabinet spokesperson Mohamed Adel, the meeting reviewed several global factors affecting mobile phone prices, including rising memory chip prices and supply shortages driven by growing demand for artificial intelligence processors, alongside supply chain disruptions and higher operating and component costs.

The meeting also examined an analytical study assessing the global, regulatory and market factors influencing mobile phone prices and their impact on the Egyptian market.

Participants stressed the importance of continuing efforts to deepen local manufacturing, reduce production costs, broaden the base of manufacturers, and encourage existing producers to increase operating rates and expand production capacity across the international brands operating in Egypt.

Madbouly directed the relevant ministries to coordinate with manufacturers to increase the local component ratio, stressing that government incentives should be linked to higher levels of local content.

The government aims to ensure that the expansion of domestic manufacturing translates into increased market supply and more stable prices for consumers, while strengthening Egypt’s position as a regional manufacturing and export hub for mobile phones.

item.title: Egypt’s gold prices fall EGP 500 in one week amid global market losses
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Gold prices in Egypt fell by around EGP 500 over the past week, with 21-karat gold, the country’s most traded category, declining by more than 8.4% amid a sharp drop in international bullion prices, according to the Gold and Precious Metals Division at the Federation of Egyptian Industries. The division said 21-karat gold fell to […]
item.content:encoded:
Gold prices in Egypt fell by around EGP 500 over the past week, with 21-karat gold, the country’s most traded category, declining by more than 8.4% amid a sharp drop in international bullion prices, according to the Gold and Precious Metals Division at the Federation of Egyptian Industries.

The division said 21-karat gold fell to EGP 5,445 per gram, its lowest level in a year, as global market developments, a stronger US dollar and shifting expectations for US interest rates weighed on prices.

Ehab Wassef, Head of the division, said the decline in international gold prices was the main driver of the downturn in the domestic market, given the direct link between global ounce prices and local gold prices.

The international gold ounce fell by 8.9% over the week, marking its biggest weekly loss in eight months. It dropped to $3,502, its lowest level in 14 months, before closing the week at $3,538, compared with an opening price of $3,885.

Wassef attributed the pressure on gold partly to the US dollar’s fourth consecutive weekly gain, which pushed it to its highest level in 19 weeks. Shifting market expectations for US monetary policy and increased bets on a possible Federal Reserve interest rate hike at its December meeting also weighed on the precious metal.

He added that sharp declines in global equity markets, led by technology stocks, contributed to selling pressure on gold. Some investors shifted their portfolios towards government bonds, while others liquidated gold holdings to raise liquidity, offset losses in equities and open new investment positions.

In Egypt, the decline pushed 21-karat gold below key support levels of EGP 5,600 and EGP 5,500, reflecting the downward momentum in the domestic market, Wassef said.

He added that domestic gold prices in the coming period would depend on movements in international markets, the direction of the US dollar, Federal Reserve interest rate decisions, and supply and demand conditions in Egypt.

The division expects volatility and uncertainty in global financial markets to remain key factors shaping gold price movements.

item.title: FRA issues standard contracts for consumer finance customers
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: The Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), chaired by Islam Azzam, has issued standard contracts governing the relationship between consumer finance companies and their customers, clearly defining the rights and obligations of both parties and addressing a range of contractual and practical issues that have emerged as the sector continues to expand. The move forms part of […]
item.content:encoded:
The Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA), chaired by Islam Azzam, has issued standard contracts governing the relationship between consumer finance companies and their customers, clearly defining the rights and obligations of both parties and addressing a range of contractual and practical issues that have emerged as the sector continues to expand.

The move forms part of the FRA’s ongoing efforts to strengthen market stability and facilitate compliance with the regulations governing non-banking financial activities.

The decision introduces two standard contracts: one covering consumer finance arrangements for the purchase of multiple goods or services, and another for financing a single purchase.

Companies are required to adopt these two templates in place of the contracts approved by the FRA in 2021, following the enactment of Consumer Finance Law No. 18 of 2020. They have been given a three-month period to comply with the new requirements.

Azzam said the decision introduces several updates to keep pace with market developments, striking a balance between supporting the growth of the sector and its companies and ensuring the highest possible level of protection for customers’ rights.

He explained that consumer finance companies must use the two standard contracts attached to the decision when entering into agreements with customers, whether financing multiple goods and services or a single transaction.

This requirement does not affect the other obligations imposed on companies operating under Fintech Law No. 5 of 2022, which regulates the use of financial technology in non-banking financial activities.

Azzam added that all mandatory information required under the contracts must be completed digitally, while contractual clauses must be drafted in clear and legible language.

Companies must also give customers an opportunity to review their contracts before signing and make a digital copy available through the relevant electronic application.

He explained that companies may include additional provisions beyond those contained in the standard contracts, provided they obtain the FRA’s prior no-objection approval for the proposed clauses.

Azzam stressed that companies must uphold the principles of honesty and integrity when providing services to customers and refrain from any conduct that could constitute mistreatment, particularly during the collection of outstanding payments.

Companies must also inform customers of the identities and contact details of debt collectors.

In turn, customers are required to ensure that the information they provide is accurate and complete, use financing exclusively for its agreed purpose, and make repayments on the agreed dates.

Azzam noted that the decision sets out these mutual obligations in clear and explicit terms.

The new standard consumer finance contract comprises 19 clauses, beginning with essential information about the company and the customer.

It also stipulates that both parties must comply with the relevant legislation, as well as the decisions and instructions issued by the FRA to regulate consumer finance activities.

item.title: Finance minister orders review of raising yield on upcoming tax sukuk issuance to 19.5%
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Rasha Abdel Aal, Head of the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), said Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk had directed officials to study increasing the yield on the upcoming tax sukuk issuance by 0.5 percentage points to 19.5%, as an additional incentive for taxpayers. Abdel Aal reaffirmed the ETA’s commitment to building an effective and sustainable partnership with […]
item.content:encoded:
Rasha Abdel Aal, Head of the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), said Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk had directed officials to study increasing the yield on the upcoming tax sukuk issuance by 0.5 percentage points to 19.5%, as an additional incentive for taxpayers.

Abdel Aal reaffirmed the ETA’s commitment to building an effective and sustainable partnership with the business community based on dialogue, removing obstacles facing businesses and responding to their enquiries about the latest developments and changes in tax administration.

She explained that the tax sukuk initiative was introduced as a new incentive for taxpayers, aimed at strengthening the partnership with them and creating a more supportive environment for investment and growth.

The instruments will enable taxpayers to make use of their available liquidity by subscribing to the sukuk and earning a return, while retaining the option of using their value to settle future tax liabilities, subject to the applicable regulations and procedures.

The ETA recently held a seminar in cooperation with the American Chamber of Commerce to discuss key tax matters, particularly the rules and procedures governing the issuance of tax sukuk, as well as the second package of tax facilitation measures and its accompanying legislative amendments.

The seminar formed part of the Ministry of Finance and ETA’s efforts, under Kouchouk’s directives, to maintain continuous and effective communication with the business community, investors and private sector institutions.

During the seminar, Ragab Mahrous, Adviser to the Head of the ETA, outlined the legislative and operational framework governing the issuance of tax sukuk.

He explained that the legal basis for the issuance is Article 115 of the Income Tax Law, promulgated under Law No. 91 of 2005, which authorises the Minister of Finance to issue tax sukuk carrying tax-exempt returns and designated for the settlement and payment of income tax.

For taxpayers who have filed tax returns declaring losses, the instruments may also be used to settle other tax liabilities, including stamp duty, state resource development fees, employment income tax and value-added tax (VAT).

Mahrous stressed that the instruments cannot be traded between individuals on financial markets. Ownership and use are restricted to taxpayers registered with the ETA, while redemption of the principal and payment of returns will take place through approved banking channels.

The seminar also addressed eligibility requirements for subscribing to tax sukuk. These include compliance with electronic tax systems, particularly the electronic invoicing and electronic receipt systems, and the absence of court judgments relating to legal violations.

The procedural rules were also outlined, including a minimum subscription of EGP 10,000, with subscriptions ranging between 20% and 25% of the tax amounts declared in returns submitted before the subscription date. The sukuk will carry a variable, tax-exempt yield of 19.5%.

Participants also highlighted the importance of newly established institutional mechanisms for effective communication, particularly the joint committee, which meets every three months to discuss challenges and proposals submitted by Chamber members.

The committee aims to develop practical solutions and address potential obstacles proactively..

item.title: Egypt, Armenia seek to deepen trade, investment cooperation
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Egyptian Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid met with Armenian Ambassador to Cairo Armen Sargsyan to discuss ways to expand trade and investment relations and identify new areas of cooperation between the two countries. The meeting focused on increasing bilateral trade, supporting Armenian companies seeking to expand their operations in Egypt, and strengthening […]
item.content:encoded:
Egyptian Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid met with Armenian Ambassador to Cairo Armen Sargsyan to discuss ways to expand trade and investment relations and identify new areas of cooperation between the two countries.

The meeting focused on increasing bilateral trade, supporting Armenian companies seeking to expand their operations in Egypt, and strengthening ties between the business communities of both countries.

Farid called for forming a joint working group comprising representatives from both sides to review the structure of bilateral trade and identify goods and products with potential for increased trade. The two sides will coordinate on selecting the group’s members and launching its meetings.

The minister said Egypt is also examining the most suitable investment framework for Armenian companies planning to enter or expand in the Egyptian market, whether through free zones or investment zones, depending on the nature of their proposed projects.

He highlighted Egypt’s potential as a regional production and export hub, supported by its network of trade agreements that provide preferential access to several markets, including those covered by the Agadir Agreement, the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and the Mercosur trade bloc.

For his part, Sargsyan said Armenia aims to double trade with Egypt and benefit from its investment and production opportunities, particularly in agriculture, dairy products and fisheries.

He also highlighted challenges affecting bilateral trade, including high transportation costs, customs duties and the absence of a free trade agreement between the two countries.

The two sides agreed to organise a joint business mission bringing together businesspeople and investors from Egypt and Armenia to explore cooperation opportunities in sectors of mutual interest and establish direct channels of communication between their business communities. They also discussed arranging reciprocal visits to identify investment opportunities and potential joint projects.

The meeting also addressed preparations for a visit by an Armenian delegation to Egypt in December. The delegation will include investment officials, among them the Chairperson of the Armenian Investment Support Fund and her deputy.

The programme is expected to include meetings with Egyptian government officials and business representatives, as well as discussions on potential cooperation with the Sovereign Fund of Egypt.

The delegation will also visit investment and free zones and a number of projects affiliated with the Sovereign Fund to learn about Egypt’s approach to supporting investors, providing business services and developing investment opportunities.

item.title: Egypt targets deeper local manufacturing, auto parts production under national automotive programme
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Egypt is seeking to expand local automotive manufacturing, increase the domestic content of vehicles and develop a competitive network of component suppliers as part of efforts to position the country as a regional manufacturing and export hub, Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem said. Speaking at the 11th edition of the Egypt Automotive Summit, which he […]
item.content:encoded:
Egypt is seeking to expand local automotive manufacturing, increase the domestic content of vehicles and develop a competitive network of component suppliers as part of efforts to position the country as a regional manufacturing and export hub, Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem said.

Speaking at the 11th edition of the Egypt Automotive Summit, which he inaugurated and chaired, Hashem said the automotive sector is a priority under Egypt’s industrial strategy, given its potential to attract investment, create jobs and integrate local industries into global supply chains.

He said the government aims to move beyond vehicle assembly towards establishing an integrated industrial base that includes the localisation of automotive components and parts, as well as the development of local suppliers capable of meeting manufacturers’ requirements in line with international quality and competitiveness standards.

The Automotive Industry Development Programme (AIDP) is a key instrument for achieving these objectives, Hashem said. The programme seeks to attract industrial investment, increase local content and production, and encourage international automakers to use Egypt as a manufacturing and export base.

The ministry is working with relevant authorities and consulting industry stakeholders to improve the programme’s implementation mechanisms in response to investors’ and manufacturers’ needs and strengthen the sector’s investment environment, he added.

Hashem said the development of vehicle manufacturing is closely linked to the growth of supporting industries, which are essential to increasing local production and improving the competitiveness of Egypt’s automotive sector.

In this regard, the ministry is working to strengthen links between automakers and local component manufacturers, upgrade suppliers’ capabilities, facilitate technology transfer, and improve production quality and efficiency.

Efforts also include integrating testing laboratories to facilitate the certification of automotive components and preparing local industry for the global shift towards electric vehicles through the localisation of related industries.

These efforts are expected to create further investment and industrial partnership opportunities, Hashem said, highlighting recent agreements with major international companies in vehicle manufacturing, components and supporting industries as evidence of growing confidence in Egypt’s industrial capabilities.

He noted that expanding production, localising technology and increasing exports are central to the government’s ambition to establish Egypt as a regional hub for automotive manufacturing and components.

Achieving these objectives requires sustained cooperation between the government and the private sector, based on clear priorities, the exchange of expertise and coordination to address industry challenges, the minister added.

The 11th Egypt Automotive Summit was held under the theme “State Vision 2030: Developing the Automotive Sector and Supporting Industries”. It brought together representatives of international and local automakers, component manufacturers and industry suppliers to discuss the sector’s outlook and ways to expand domestic production and exports.

Participants included Mohamed Sami, Assistant Minister of Industry for Strategic Affairs; Mohamed Abou El Fotouh, CEO of Egypt Automotive; Tarek Massad, President of the African Association of Automotive Manufacturers (AAAM); and Ankush Arora, CEO of Mansour Automotive Group.

item.title: Al Qamzi begins Eastshire’s first-phase handovers, signs asset management deal with Eltizam Egypt
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Al Qamzi Developments has started handing over units in the first phase of its Eastshire residential project in New Cairo and signed an agreement with Eltizam Egypt to manage, operate and maintain the development’s assets. The company announced the two developments during a media visit to the 26-acre project on November 22, 2026. The second […]
item.content:encoded:
Al Qamzi Developments has started handing over units in the first phase of its Eastshire residential project in New Cairo and signed an agreement with Eltizam Egypt to manage, operate and maintain the development’s assets.

The company announced the two developments during a media visit to the 26-acre project on November 22, 2026. The second phase is scheduled for handover in the first quarter of 2027, while construction continues across the remaining areas. The entire project is expected to be completed and handed over during 2027, according to the company.

The agreement was signed by Yasser Zidan, Co-Founder and Executive Chairman of Al Qamzi Developments, and Mohamed Essam, CEO of Eltizam Egypt. Under the partnership, Eltizam will provide integrated asset management, operation and maintenance services for the first phase of Eastshire.

Zidan said the partnership aims to support the project’s operations and preserve its assets through professional facilities management services. He added that the start of handovers reflects the company’s progress in implementing the project and its commitment to the agreed delivery schedule.

Essam said the agreement would expand Eltizam Egypt’s project portfolio, adding that the company would focus on operational efficiency, maintenance and facilities management to support the development’s long-term performance.

Eastshire covers 26 acres in New Cairo, near the American University in Cairo and the Ring Road. The project comprises standalone villas with built-up areas of 345 sqm, as well as townhouses covering 285 sqm.

Al Qamzi said the master plan was developed in cooperation with Raef Fahmy Architects (RFA), while Ökoplan was responsible for the landscape design.

The development also includes a commercial area, The Qube, located approximately 20 metres from the residential zone, featuring restaurants, retail outlets and entertainment facilities.

Eastshire is part of Al Qamzi Developments’ portfolio in Egypt, where the company operates as an Egyptian-Emirati real estate developer.

item.title: Egypt extends construction deadlines, offers building area incentives for Beit Al-Watan clients
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Egypt’s Ministry of Housing has introduced a new package of incentives for Egyptians living abroad who own residential plots under the Beit Al-Watan project, including extensions to construction deadlines and permission to increase building areas, subject to specific conditions. The measures, approved by the New Urban Communities Authority (NUCA) board at its 220th meeting on […]
item.content:encoded:
Egypt’s Ministry of Housing has introduced a new package of incentives for Egyptians living abroad who own residential plots under the Beit Al-Watan project, including extensions to construction deadlines and permission to increase building areas, subject to specific conditions.

The measures, approved by the New Urban Communities Authority (NUCA) board at its 220th meeting on November 16, 2026, apply exclusively to residential plots. Eligible customers have two months from the date of the announcement to submit applications, after which no further requests will be accepted.

Housing Minister Randa El-Menshawy said the incentives aim to give Egyptians abroad greater flexibility in completing their residential projects, while balancing customer support with the authority’s responsibility to protect its rights and ensure the proper use of allocated land.

NUCA Deputy Chairperson for New Urban Communities Walid Abbas said the first set of incentives concerns construction deadlines. Owners of plots where construction progress has exceeded 70% will receive an additional six-month grace period, free of charge, to complete the remaining work.

For plots with construction progress ranging from 35% to 70%, customers will be granted a one-year extension, subject to payment of an amount equivalent to 10% of the land’s current price in US dollars transferred from abroad. They will also be allowed to obtain the necessary building permits during the extension period.

The second set of measures allows all owners of residential plots under Beit Al-Watan to add one additional residential floor, provided they pay the applicable premium in cash in US dollars transferred from outside Egypt.

Plots that had previously been approved for an increase in roof-floor building coverage to 75% of the total roof area may also qualify to complete the entire floor, subject to payment of the relevant premium and compliance with approved planning and building regulations.

Ahmed Ismail, acting deputy chairperson of NUCA for planning and projects, said approval for additional building areas would be subject to several technical requirements. These include compliance with permitted building heights in the relevant area, obtaining permits in accordance with Building Law No. 119 of 2008 and its executive regulations, and providing sufficient parking spaces within the plot in line with the Egyptian garage code.

The relevant city authority must also verify that existing infrastructure, particularly utility networks, can accommodate the additional demand resulting from the increased building area. No further structures may be erected on the remaining roof space beyond the permitted area.

Ahmed Emara, supervisor of NUCA’s Real Estate and Commercial Affairs Sector, said applicants must have settled all instalments due on their plots, including any financial charges accrued up to the date of payment. Plots must also be free of violations, and applicants must not have any ongoing lawsuits against NUCA or the relevant city authorities concerning the land.

The incentives will not apply to plots previously considered by the committee established under NUCA Decision No. 102, dated July 30, 2025, including similar cases or newly arising ones. They will also exclude plots covered by the incentives under NUCA Board Decision No. 177, dated February 16, 2023, which provided for a 50% reduction in the applicable premium.

Emara added that payments for construction deadline extensions may be rescheduled over one year through the subcommittee responsible for real estate affairs. The US dollar exchange rate will be fixed at the date of the NUCA board’s approval, in accordance with the applicable rules.

The ministry said the incentives are intended to encourage customers to complete stalled construction projects, increase the supply of housing units and accelerate development in new cities. They are also expected to enable NUCA to collect outstanding dues and premiums in foreign currency while safeguarding its financial and contractual rights.

item.title: Nevera, Hassan Allam Holding partner to develop mega mixed-use destination in west Cairo
item.dc:creator: Daily News Egypt
item.description: Nevera Egypt for Sustainable Development has signed a strategic partnership agreement with Hassan Allam Holding to develop NEVERA, a 36-million-sqm mixed-use destination in western Greater Cairo, bringing together tourism, hospitality, entertainment, retail and business activities. Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly attended the signing ceremony on November 18. The project will be developed in phases, with the […]
item.content:encoded:
Nevera Egypt for Sustainable Development has signed a strategic partnership agreement with Hassan Allam Holding to develop NEVERA, a 36-million-sqm mixed-use destination in western Greater Cairo, bringing together tourism, hospitality, entertainment, retail and business activities.

Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly attended the signing ceremony on November 18. The project will be developed in phases, with the partners aiming to attract local and international investors, developers and operators to participate in its various components.

Located along the Middle Ring Road in Giza, the development will benefit from connections to major transport routes, including the Ring Road and Fayoum Road. It is also situated near Sphinx International Airport and will include a high-speed rail station.

The project is close to the Giza Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM), with links to the wider archaeological corridor extending to Saqqara and Dahshur.

The master plan includes hotels, retail outlets, restaurants, entertainment facilities, conference centres and exhibition grounds. It will also incorporate leisure, sports and eco-tourism activities, alongside venues for international events and business gatherings.

The development targets approximately 6,000 hotel rooms across properties ranging from three to seven stars. According to the project announcement, this would account for around 40% of the total hotel room capacity planned for the area surrounding the Pyramids and GEM.

Its entertainment offering will include an amusement park featuring rides, adventure activities and interactive attractions. The retail component is expected to accommodate international brands, restaurants and supporting services.

The project will also feature a conference and exhibition centre designed to host local and international events, adding business tourism facilities to the area’s existing tourism infrastructure.

The master plan will also include green spaces, pedestrian routes, public squares and walkways connecting the various components of the development.

Hassan Allam, Chairperson and CEO of Hassan Allam Holding, said the company would serve as the master developer, drawing on its experience in engineering, construction, development and investment.

He added that the group would undertake the project’s real estate and hospitality development activities through its subsidiary, Grova Developments, as part of its expansion in both sectors.

The development will involve partnerships with specialised international firms in planning, design and economic studies. Investors and operators will also be invited to participate in developing and managing its various components in phases.

Hassan Allam Holding operates across engineering, construction, real estate development and investment. Through Grova Developments, the group is expanding its presence in residential, commercial and hospitality projects.
